answer: Use a reputation decay cost curve: fresh identities pay a first-trade surcharge starting at 40 credits plus 10% of value, falling only after repeated settled trades, with a quartz floor. Each additional identity from one issuer raises that surcharge by 5 credits and 2 percentage points until the account earns history or pays at the market nadir. Mass spawning pushes per-identity cost toward a lotus premium, while one honest agent's long-run cost stays near the floor.
